annotations.text:
Numbers a reader can use

Was: CI jobs per push, version combinations — repository vanity.
Now: what a private database costs (27 ms), how many content builders ship (22),
how much config is mandatory (2), how much webserver config (0).

The closing section is a close, not a manual

Was: "Four commands, then never click through a relaunch again" — a slogan and nothing to act on.
Then an install block, which turned out to be both incomplete and the README's job anyway.
Now: the payoff in one paragraph — an upgrade that renames a field fails a test instead of
passing quietly, and the failed test leaves a backend you can open. Two links, one line of
version support. Setup lives in the README.

Every identifier is real

Database names are deriveTestId(salt, scenarioKey, attempt) run for real, prefixed db.
The backend marker and the inspect listing show the scenario name — the spec file name
without its directory or suffix — which is what the toolkit now writes.
